fundLockMechanism: This entry exists because an incident named "Perfect Finance" (2023, ~$3M) appears in FLARE's early design references. Searched public reporting on 2026-09-11 with several query variants — ["Perfect Finance" DeFi hack exploit 2023 protocol], ["Perfect Finance" crypto $3 million exploit rekt], [rekt.news "Perfect Finance"], ["PerfectSwap" OR "Perfect Vault" OR "PerfectFi" defi exploit 2023] — checking DeFi hack trackers (Koinly, Blockworks, ChainSec, Frontal), the rekt.news leaderboard directly, and general web search. None returned a protocol named "Perfect Finance" (or a plausible close variant) with a 2023 incident; the closest name matches (Grim Finance, Team Finance, MM Finance) are unrelated hacks. Rather than invent a plausible-sounding root cause to fill the slot, this is labeled unverified and excluded from every FLARE statistic.

amount.note: The $3M figure from the original design reference has no corroborating source we could locate and is not repeated here as fact.

limitations: This case study could not be verified against public reporting as of the research date (re-checked 2026-09-11 with multiple targeted search queries — see fundLockMechanism — with no new result). It is retained, clearly flagged, rather than silently dropped, so the gap is visible — and it is excluded from every aggregate figure FLARE displays (the 'affected in case studies' total, taxonomy counts used for marketing copy, etc.). A fifth, better-documented incident was deliberately not substituted in its place: four independently-verified case studies already give the taxonomy real diversity, and swapping this entry for a cleaner-looking one would remove the visible evidence that not every claim in an early design reference could be corroborated — which is itself a useful, honest data point about working from secondhand references. If you have a primary source for this incident, FLARE's data model supports upgrading its verification status once one is added.
